frictionPoints.title: Build and test a prototype

frictionPoints.title: Understand the market
frictionPoints.text: Explore customer needs, alternatives, pricing and possible routes to reach the people who may use the solution.

journey.title: Identify a problem
journey.text: Observe a real need, speak with people who experience it and describe the problem clearly.
journey.output: A focused problem statement and early observations.

journey.title: Build a team
journey.text: Bring together complementary strengths, agree on a shared purpose and define responsibilities.
journey.output: A committed team with clear ownership.

journey.title: Shape the idea
journey.text: Explore possible approaches, identify the intended users and decide what needs to be tested first.
journey.output: A clear concept and a testable assumption.

journey.title: Create a prototype
journey.text: Build a simple first version and use small experiments to learn what works and what needs improvement.
journey.output: A demonstrable prototype and learning notes.

journey.title: Validate with users
journey.text: Gather feedback from relevant users and practitioners, then refine the solution using evidence.
journey.output: User feedback and a more grounded solution.

journey.title: Present the next step
journey.text: Summarise the problem, team, prototype, feedback and next milestones in a clear presentation.
journey.output: A practical plan for continued development.

about.title: A platform for builders, not just business plans.
about.description: The Entrepreneurship Development Cell at KPRCAS makes entrepreneurship a practical, collaborative and accessible part of the student experience.
about.story: Established in 2020, the Entrepreneurship Development Cell has grown as a student-led platform for exposure, experimentation and enterprise. It creates opportunities for students to learn by doing, collaborate across disciplines, connect with mentors and translate real-world problems into purposeful solutions.
about.mission: Build an entrepreneurial mindset through practical experiences, strong teams, access to mentors and a supportive innovation ecosystem.
about.vision: Enable a generation of confident, responsible creators who build relevant solutions and contribute to society and the economy.

blogs.title: Why the strongest startup idea begins with a real problem
blogs.author: EDC Editorial Desk
blogs.excerpt: A useful idea does more than sound exciting. It responds to a problem people recognise and are willing to solve.
blogs.body:
Begin with observation, not assumptions. Talk to people who experience the problem, map the workarounds they already use and understand what a better outcome would mean to them.

A first solution is a hypothesis. A good team tests that hypothesis in small, low-cost ways, learns from the evidence and improves its approach.

The discipline of asking better questions is often more valuable than rushing towards a polished pitch. Build the habit of learning before scaling.

blogs.title: Team formation is a founder skill
blogs.author: EDC Editorial Desk
blogs.excerpt: A committed team creates the capacity to turn ambition into sustained execution.
blogs.body:
A venture needs more than a collection of enthusiastic people. It needs shared intent, clear responsibilities, complementary strengths and an honest way to make decisions.

Start with a small experiment together. Notice how people communicate, handle uncertainty and follow through. Define ownership early, revisit roles as the idea develops and build trust through consistent action.

A good team is not found fully formed. It is built deliberately.

blogs.title: From prototype to pilot: what should a team learn?
blogs.author: EDC Editorial Desk
blogs.excerpt: A pilot is not just a demonstration. It is a structured opportunity to gather evidence.
blogs.body:
A prototype helps a team make an idea tangible. A pilot helps the team understand whether the solution works in a real context.

Define what you need to learn before you begin. Choose a small group of relevant users, decide how you will observe outcomes and document both positive and negative signals.

Use the findings to improve the product, rethink the customer or decide whether to continue. Evidence is progress.
